Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood CSM) -- Priya Singh (Head of ML), Carlos Ramos (Platform Eng), Evelyn Park (FinOps) -- Recording auto captions

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage, cost decomposition, and how Redwood's routing/batching/caching levers can reduce unit cost. Customer concerned about predictable billing for inference-heavy clinical features and securing PHI in a hybrid setup. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot and exchange logs for baseline metrics.

Topics:
- Route dashboards and custom tags
- Cost breakdown per route / per-model
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, SSO
- Next steps: pricing, pilot, benchmark run

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I run the AE for healthcare accounts, quick roll call?
[00:09] Priya: hi Priya here, Head of ML at Orchid Health. joining from SF, yep
[00:13] Carlos: Carlos, platform eng, late afternoon here, thanks
[00:16] Evelyn: Evelyn, FinOps, quick note I'm mostly concerned about billing granularity
[00:21] Maya: perfect. Liam from our infra team will do most of the console walkthrough, i'll chime on business and security items.
[00:27] Liam: hey all, i'll share my screen, give me a sec. (screen share noise) okay can you see the console?
[00:34] Priya: yep i see it, the landing page looks clean
[00:37] Liam: cool. first thing — this is the usage overview, top-left you can pick time ranges and group by route or model. we built it so teams can map features to routes, so your triage assistant vs clinical-notes extraction show up separately.
[00:51] Carlos: can you tag routes by environment — prod vs staging?
[00:55] Liam: yes, we support route metadata and custom tags; you can also auto-infer tags from the SDK if you pass metadata fields.
[01:05] Maya: customers use that to split FinOps chargebacks. Evelyn, this is the part that usually helps teams map costs to product teams.
[01:12] Evelyn: nice. can you show per-route cost breakdown?
[01:15] Liam: sure, switching to the per-route dashboard. note: costs here are computed from tokens + model profiles + GPU runtime adjustments; there's a small lag for final invoice reconciliation but it's within 24 hours for hosted.
[01:30] (screen pause, faint typing)
[01:35] Liam: so this view shows top routes by spend, average latency, p50/p95, and the model used. you can click a route and drill to per-model and per-time-slice.
[01:46] Priya: that token + model profile mapping — is that configurable? we have two models in prod, a fast small model for routing and a larger one for clinical summarization.
[01:56] Liam: yep, you can pin which model each route uses, and also define fallback policies — for example, if the large model is saturated, fallback to a quantized variant or to a lower-cost region.
[02:07] Carlos: how granular is the chargeback? we want hourly rollups to feed into our billing pipeline.
[02:13] Liam: you can export hourly CSVs with route, model, token counts, latency stats — there's an export API and S3 sink for large volumes.
[02:22] Evelyn: do you have examples of mapping to our internal cost buckets? we need to show per-feature monthly cost to execs.
[02:29] Maya: yes, we usually provide a mapping guide and a sample BigQuery schema you can plug into your data warehouse. we'll attach that.
[02:36] Priya: cool. show us the routing/optimization suggestions you mentioned earlier?
[02:41] Liam: right — this is Redwood Optimize. it surfaces suggestions: batching thresholds, caching prefixes, and quantization recommendations per-model. here's an example rule: if route avg tokens < 200, recommend int4 quantization on that model and a batch size of 8 to reduce GPU time.
[02:57] Priya: int4 — are there quality regressions we should worry about for clinical text?
[03:02] Liam: good question. Optimize ties each suggestion to a recent evaluation set. you'll see an estimated quality delta (we show rouge/response similarity metrics). for sensitive clinical outputs we recommend running a small eval set first; we can help with that.
[03:17] Carlos: do we need to change inference code to use caching?
[03:22] Liam: minimal changes — the SDK has a cache middleware. for prefix caching you can mark tokens as cacheable at request time. it also supports shared K/V cache in Dedicated.
[03:32] Evelyn: speaking of Dedicated — what's the SLA and cost delta vs hosted?
[03:37] Maya: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, better isolation. pricing is a monthly commit — we'll include a sample TCO comparison. usually customers with consistent > X tokens/month gravitate to Dedicated.
[03:49] Priya: our busiest endpoint is summarization — bursty but sustained. we want to avoid cold starts during spikes.
[03:56] Liam: autoscaling policies with warm pools can handle that. also we recommend prefix/KV caching to smooth spikes.
[04:04] (brief cross-talk)
[04:09] Priya: security: we process PHI, can we run in our VPC and bring our own KMS?
[04:15] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports customer VPC deployments and KMS/HSM integrations. we also provide an on-prem package if you need air-gapped.
[04:23] Carlos: and audit logs?
[04:26] Maya: full audit trails, per-request trace IDs, retention configurable. we'll share an export sample.
[04:33] Evelyn: SOC2? data residency?
[04:36] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II; for residency we have region options and Private deployments for strict controls. we'll include the compliance pack after the call.
[04:46] Priya: any integrations for SSO? we use Okta and SCIM.
[04:49] Liam: SAML, OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC in the console.
[04:55] Carlos: latency numbers — can you show p50/p95 for the models?
[05:00] Liam: here's the latency pane. note that p95 includes queuing during bursts; we also surface per-host metrics. for the quantized variants p50 improves but quality estimates vary.
[05:12] Priya: about fallback routing — how easy is it to set a cost cap per route so it never exceeds $X/day?
[05:19] Liam: you can set cost thresholds that trigger automated fallbacks or rate-limits; the console will also surface alerts to Slack/email.
[05:28] Evelyn: perfect — we need those alerts tied to our FinOps channel.
[05:31] Maya: we can set that up in the pilot.
[05:34] (screen scroll)
[05:36] Liam: next i'll show a small demo of drilling into a route: click route -> time series -> token distribution -> export button. here's an export we've prepared for a demo customer (slightly obfuscated).
[05:49] Priya: the export includes model variant names?
[05:51] Liam: yes, model id, variant, quantization profile.
[05:55] Carlos: can we map that to our internal model names?
[05:58] Liam: you can set aliases via the API, so mapping is straightforward.
[06:03] (10 min jump, system note: stuttering and background noises)
[16:20] Priya: sorry jumped back — question about burst costs if we use Hosted and suddenly double traffic; any safety nets?
[16:27] Maya: there are policy controls: reserve burst capacity, set spend caps and automated fallbacks. also support for pre-warming for scheduled events.
[16:35] Carlos: what about noisy neighbours in hosted?
[16:38] Liam: we isolate workloads with container-level cgroups and continuous batching to avoid noisy-neighbor effects; Dedicated eliminates noisy tenants entirely.
[16:46] Evelyn: on the finance side we need a sample invoice line items — token counts vs runtime vs model premium.
[16:55] Maya: we'll send a sample invoice that breaks out tokens, embedding units, model multiplier, and any Dedicated capacity fees.
[17:01] Priya: curious — do you support model rollouts / canarying per-route?
[17:07] Liam: yes, per-route canaries, A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions. rollouts can be percent-based and time-windowed.
[17:15] Carlos: do you have a feature flag integration?
[17:18] Liam: we have integrations with LaunchDarkly and split-based routing in the SDK.
[17:22] (short pause)
[17:27] Priya: what kind of metrics are available for quality monitoring?
[17:31] Liam: you can attach eval sets to routes, Redwood will compute similarity/ROUGE-type scores and surface regressions and alerts.
[17:39] Evelyn: do you store prompts and outputs? we have privacy constraints.
[17:43] Maya: default hosted mode retains request metadata for 30 days for debugging; Private deployments can give you full control. we support redaction policies and request-level encryption.
[17:54] Priya: that retention might be an issue for PHI, we'll look at Private options.
[17:59] Carlos: ok can we talk about the pilot? timeline?
[18:03] Maya: typically a 2-week pilot: week 1 baseline ingest and small perf runs, week 2 optimizations and cost modeling. we'll need a representative traffic sample and some eval prompts.
[18:15] Priya: we can provide a week's logs and a 200-sample eval set.
[18:19] Evelyn: and who will be our day-to-day contact?
[18:22] Maya: Jordan will be your CSM, Liam for technical, and i'll own commercial. Jordan can run onboarding.
[18:30] Jordan: thanks — i'll follow up with an onboarding checklist and the pilot runbook.
[18:35] (background typing)
[18:40] Carlos: one more — competitor question: we evaluated Replicate and a managed OpenAI approach, how is Redwood different?
[18:47] Maya: our focus is production inference controls: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, predictable SLAs, and per-route economics tooling. we also emphasize observability and auto optimization tooling (Optimize) that generates actionable batching/caching recommendations.
[19:03] Priya: sounds good. any case studies for healthcare?
[19:07] Maya: yes, we have a de-identified case study; we'll share links after call.
[19:12] Carlos: ok next steps and responsibilities?
[19:15] Maya: quick recap — Redwood to send security pack, TCO sample, pilot runbook, and pricing. Orchid to share logs, target routes, and eval set.
[19:26] Priya: will do.
[19:28] Evelyn: expecting the billing export format sample please.
[19:31] Maya: we'll include it in the email.
[19:33] Jordan: i'll send calendar invites for the kickoff next Tuesday.
[19:36] (wrap)
[19:38] Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the time.
[19:41] Priya: thanks all, bye
[19:43] Carlos: thanks
[19:44] Evelyn: bye
